Controlled, Astoria repeated the word in her mind, is this what all of my life has been so far?
What had she done to be controlled? Were they going to torture her? What had she done? Nothing. She was weak. Even if she had some distant relation to those people, to him, did it matter? She was no one. She had always been no one.
Next Wednesday came. Astoria hesitated to visit Harry. It was a tough week for both of them. It felt like a parallel universe, as if they switched who they were.
Harry was an outcast. Many though he cheated his way somehow to put his name in the goblet. They blamed him for trying to steal the spotlight, yet again, from another student. Slytherins spread some kind of badges and other stuff to bully Harry. They sold like freshly baked bread. No one supported him and all the other houses were against him.
And Astoria was looked with curiosity by everyone. Seeing those wizards, the fear they commanded, it made an impression. Her peers distanced themselves from her. No one wanted to sit next to her, curious looks surrounded her and at one point it occurred to her that they feared her. Maybe admired her from afar. It was a complicated feeling, mostly they were all confused about her as some noticed her for the first time. No matter what, she was always looked at.
It even got Draco’s attention. They’d separate them into small groups when working on complicated potions. He specifically came to her. This was in a way to assert his dominance. In Slytherin everything was about connections and blood. Suddenly there was a rumor she came from a far more powerful family than him. A cruel joke to her but Astoria still hoped it stung him, at least a bit.
At the beginning there was only a discussion about school projects, gathering ingredients and arguing how to mix them. The worst part was that Pansy Parkinson was with them.
'I hope now you realize you are a Slytherin', Draco Malfoy suddenly said to her.
'I know what I am', Astoria lied.
'Good, because a name doesn’t make you special', Pansy hissed as she looked her from her head to toes, 'Surly, the disappointment of the family'.
But there was no family. They were all dead, from what she knew. And she was alone, now with a different name. That was all.
'It is a powerful name', Draco admitted, 'And it explains why Dumbledore himself kept you close for so long'.
It actually made zero sense to Astoria.
'You think I’m some kind of secret ace, but I’m going to disappoint you. He takes no interest in me. The way I see it, he took me in out of compassion, not for some great plot'.
'And it’s a coincidence you and Potter are friends?'
'That is no coincidence. He is just kind to me.'
Pansy rolled her eyes.
'Maybe you should marry him. Since the two of you are so in love'
'I said we’re friends, not in love', Astoria corrected her.
Draco grabbed her hand to pull her close. His mouth opened next to her ear and his breath tingled her skin. He wanted to tell her something, but Astoria felt repulsed by the closeness they shared suddenly in this moment, and she flinched instantly. His grip tightened quickly. It all happened so fast and she couldn’t hide it from him as a whimper from the pain left her lips.
He instantly pulled back and looked somehow confused.
'I didn’t mean to hurt you. Are you okay?'
The way he said it surprised both girls. Astoria couldn’t believe it but there was softness in his voice. It was almost like he was being nice. Pansy looked unhappy as she put her hand on his shoulder and ran her fingers on his neck. Draco didn’t flinch but he didn’t react in any way either.
'Thank you, I’m fine', Astoria said politely. She was so used to hating him it felt out of place to be nice back.
'You don’t like it, do you?', he kept talking to her with curiosity in his voice.
'What do you mean?'
'You don’t like being pureblood, being an Elroy'
It was a true observation. That name meant nothing to her. And it put her in danger, if so many people thought there was some significance to it.
'I think people are exaggerating.'
'They’re not', he cut her off and then smirked, 'I should teach you some things. What being an aristocrat truly means'.
Astoria blinked back as no words came to her. He’d never spoken to her like that. It was almost as if he didn’t hate her. That was in a way worse, she realized. Pansy was already throwing knifes at her with her eyes.
'She wouldn’t know what that means even if you carve it in her brain', she snorted and rolled her eyes.
It was mockery, but Astoria had no smart-comments to throw back at her. Her face was blushing and she didn’t even know why. It felt more embarrassing than any humiliation Draco Malfoy had done to her, so she just ignored Pansy and her jokes and tried to hide away in a textbook.
The conversation stuck to her. Astoria thought about Draco’s words throughout the day. What did it mean to be a Slytherin? She knew from Harry it was a mark to set you off for a dark path. Yet power wasn’t always dark, right?
Power corrupts, she noted to herself with shame. And it didn’t matter because she had no power. Not really.
One sleepless night she sneaked out of bed. The empty corridors of the schools betrayed her with an echo attached to every step she took. The library was locked but that made zero sense in a school about magic. Astoria imagined an honorable Gryffindor would turn away, or maybe a naïve Hufflepuff.  But she was neither.
Revelio, she whispered with a quick movement with a wand.
That night she tried to search for her name.
Elroy. From king. An ancient family name, mostly associated with two distinguished traits – the red eyes, that marked a wizard’s connection to the dark arts, and pyromancy. She was afraid of fire, ironically. Astoria had never cast a single flame, neither she suspected being able to do so.
The man she saw, that appeared to be so feared, he died long before she was born. He wasn’t her father, if she did the math correctly, he was old enough to be her grandfather but she doubt that. Instead, she was probably some distant offspring to some bastard of god knows who. It was chance that she looked like him. Maybe it was the hair. She wasn’t even sure she had any relations to him at all.
Now the notion seemed absurd to her. To be an Elroy. To be connected in any way to those people she saw. She was a girl also, and Dumbledore had said that somehow mattered. Made her weak.
Everyone else hadn’t reach this realization yet, thankfully for Astoria. The bullying stopped. They all looked at her as if she was about to snap and lose her mind in class. Maybe that was a possibility.
There was very little information other than that. Some old pictures of people who looked nothing like her and the rest seemed to be hidden away.
After a few nights she slipped away one more time from Slytherin’s dorm. Harry was already waiting for her.
'Sorry if I’m late. Pansy stayed up late glaring at me with hate and I couldn’t leave.'
'It’s okay', Harry smiled.
It all seamed fake to her. His smile, the way he looked at her, all that happened so far. Nothing was real, maybe she had died and was in Hell.
'I’m sorry also for the hate you get. I believe you didn’t put your name in the goblet.'
'Thank you, I rarely hear it', he confessed and sadness darkened his green eyes.
'I don’t know', Harry sounded tired, 'I suspect someone loyal to Voldemort'.
'Being a champion in games with a high risk on your life sure sounds as something he would wish. But who?'
'Dumbledore suspects it as well. He told me to watch out, but I think even he hasn’t figured out who did it. I thought about Igor Karakoff, however he seems focused on you.'
It stinged her. Dumbledore often spoke with Harry and at times it seemed to her he knew more about everything then she did. He still hadn’t spoken with her. It hurt. It hurt because she knew he saw her crying and he knew how much it would hurt. The public humiliation. They talked about her issues to fit in once and he did nothing to make it easier for her.
Caged, she reminded herself and her thoughts went silent. No one had put her in a cage, but she suspected it was a metaphor for something else. Dumbledore told them she was already controlled.  She never viewed her life like that before, yet it did make sense.
'Did you know it was Moody who put him in Azkaban?', Harry seemed to be studying her reactions as his eyes were stuck on her. She shook her head.
Her face must’ve gave her away because Harry suddenly changed the topic.
'Tori, I need you to know I don’t think you’re evil.'
'Thank you, but you were right. If I really share blood with those –, with that man, I come from a long line of dark wizards. It would be natural for me to be in Slytherin and it would be expected if one day I–'
He stopped her. Both his arms were on her shoulder. She lost her words. He said something, but she was suddenly deaf. He had consuming eyes. Green with a spark, yet a beautiful dark shade of the color. Like a forest to lose yourself in.
'Did you hear me?', Harry repeated, 'I don’t believe any of that.'
Somehow, she now was even more convinced it was true.
'What are you going to do about the Tournament?', she asked suddenly in despair to take back the conversation towards him.
His hands left her, and the cold air took their place. She shivered. Harry noticed but didn’t reach out again. He looked through the window in the forest.
'I’m going to train and compete. I have no choice. Ron thinks I cheated and is somehow mad at me', he sounded irritated.
'He’s jealous', Astoria said coldly, 'He’s insecurities always get the best of him and that makes him a liability to you. Maybe this is for the best.'
He clearly didn’t share her opinion as he looked at her with disbelief, almost disgust. He loved them, Ron and Hermione, he loved them more than her. She knew and she figured in this instant that it was maybe she who was jealous.
'Don’t ever say that again', Harry said, to her surprise, softly, 'he is my friend. I know why you might think that, but you are wrong. I know Ron can be an ass, a pain in the ass, but he is my friend and I know that in my heart'.
'I hope you are right and he also finds the same in his heart', Astoria tried to response as emotionless as possible, yet her sarcasm was still visible. Harry chose to ignore it. They had other subjects on which they never met eye to eye, this wasn’t new.
'He will. It will take some time, but he will.'
'Who is training you?'
'Alastor Moody. He volunteered to help me', then after some quiet seconds he added, 'I think I want to be an auror one day.'
'I wish you the best for that', Astoria said. It would suit him perfectly. And he would probably look very handsome in those uniforms they had -
'Have you given it any thought?'
'To be an auror?'
'Maybe. Anything, really? '
The question caught her off guard. Astoria stood silent for a minute. She never actually thought about that. There was no life after Hogwarts in her mind. She was always stuck here. Caged.
'I don’t think I’ll live that long', she confessed and flushed red as it was somehow embarrassing for her to be this vulnerable.
'Don’t say that!', Harry almost shouted and she shushed him. 'You’re being dramatic.'
She didn’t response. He knew she wasn’t being dramatic. They never discussed it before, she never brought it up and it somehow seemed wrong to do so now. It was a mistake in her part.
'I can’t explain it, but I an certain of it', the words slowly leaving her lips.
'I sometimes feel as if I’m not going to live long as well', Harry said quietly, 'But I need to, for my friends and for those I love. Sometimes I think I won’t make it. In my fears Voldemort wins.'
That was new to her. Fear was never an emotion she associated to Harry. Reckless, stupidly brave, naïve, careless – that was him, no debate there. But now Astoria recognized doubt he buried deep in his heart.
'You already defeated him once. As a baby. Then stopped all his attempts to hurt you. You will do it again', Astoria meant it and that eased Harry a bit.
'I know, I don’t think there is another choice', Harry said with obvious sadness and then looked up to her and surprisingly added, 'I think you will make a good auror as well.'
'I don’t think so', Astoria chuckled.
'Moody told me he could train you as well. For a bit, just to learn to control your power.'
Astoria blinked in disbelief.
'How? Dumbledore, he – ', she said, not understanding what he meant.
'Together. Tomorrow in his office, after class. And Dumbledore knows, he proposed it'.
Her eyes lowered with sadness. More secrets that she had to learn through his favorite child – Harry fucking Potter.
'He still hasn’t spoken to me'.
'He will come around, I’m sure', said Harry and smiled sincerely.
The last class for the day was potions with Snape. Harry always hated the class, as well as everyone else expect Draco Malfoy who seemed to be the professor’s favorite. They pared Astoria with him as well as Theo Nott on a healing potion.
Draco was looking at Harry. When their eyes met he ran a finger across his neck and whispered 'Good luck, Potter'. Snape noticed Harry’s anger and slapped him on the head with the cover of a book. Then raised an eyebrow towards Draco and called him with a gesture.
Theo and Astoria were left alone, waiting for the potion to brew.
'Have you given it any thought?' he suddenly said. She didn’t quite understand that.
'Of course, everything is according to the textbook. We should be okay', she said affirmative, but she wasn’t sure if this was the correct answer to his question.
'No', he chuckled, and two dimples formed on his face. He had beautiful, big eyes that always seemed sincere to Astoria. She always thought he was probably a great liar. A natural advantage in Slytherin.
'Are you going to the Yule Ball?'
'I –, I guess I am', Astoria answered. She stepped back as she felt her face turn red. She hadn’t thought about the ball at all recently.
In fact she avoided the event in her mind and on her calendar because she was sure she wouldn’t go. That was better than suffering the humiliation of going alone and standing in the corner all night, watching everyone else have fun and dance and kiss and all other normal things teenagers did.
'Do you have someone to go with?', he got closer to her.
Theodore wasn’t exceptionally tall like Draco or Blaise but had a large frame. Everyone who played Quidditch seemed in a great shape but being athletic was more a natural advantage to him. Like his sincere eyes that probably covered all his lies.
Her head was spinning. No one had asked her before. Not that there was any similar event before, but even if there were, Astoria was sure this would be the first time someone would ask her. Theo smiled, seemingly enjoying watching her blush. His hand reached for her and she tried to move, to do something – anything really.
Their hands met and he gave her a shy smile. He had rough palms that indicated a tight grip and unlike Harry who only barely touched her skin with the tips of his fingers as if he’d burn himself, Theo seemingly wasn’t afraid of fire. It was Draco Malfoy who separated them in that moment. He pushed trough them and then looked at each them raising one perfect eyebrow on his face.
'What is going on? Am I interrupting something?', he said towards Theo who smiled back at him kindly and shook his head.
'We were just checking the potion’s mixture. All well, according to textbook, right?'
A great liar, indeed, Astoria nodded, watching him wink playfully to her. She thought she was pretty good at lying as well, yet words just couldn’t come out. When Draco turned to stare her down with his icy blue eyes, she just looked away, hoping he wouldn’t notice her red cheeks.
'Don’t forget all students have a scheduled meeting in one hour with the Head of the House for preparation for the Yule Ball', Snape announced then looked around all Slytherin students as his eyes squinted, 'Don’t. Be. Late'.
Theo approached Astoria and Draco seemingly tried to block him. However, she didn’t notice as her eyes widened with the realization that she probably won’t make it.
'Fuck', she said to herself while both turned to look at her with surprise. No explanation was provided on her side as she had just stormed out of the room.
Alastor 'Mad-Eye' Moody. The nickname did strike fear but seeing it up close was terrifying. Astoria and Harry stood awkwardly next to each other, trying not to be rude by staring. Only there was no way not to stare.
He looked back at them for a long time. Almost like a test who will flinch away first. Astoria felt that could be unpolite and bit her tongue but did not move. And Harry was a Gryffindor, bravery was a must there.
Alastor Moody came closer, studying both with his synthetic eye that circled and twisted in a terrifying way. Blaise Zabini said one time between classes to the boys that Moody could detect dark magic with his eye. Those words came to Astoria immediately and panic filled her. Maybe he could see it in her and then there would be no room for doubt. Her future – doomed.
'I never met him', Moody finally said.
'Who?', Astoria asked as her voice trembled.
'Your supposed grandfather. The last flame.', Moody said calmly as the words sank into her. 'I don’t know any of his techniques to practice with you. The last living person who has ever fought your grandfather and lived, he, well, that’s not an option'.
Astoria stood frozen and silent, swallowing his words. It felt as if the training had already begin and she was already bleeding, naked and vulnerable.
'We’ll have to figure out what to do with the dragons', Moody suddenly turned towards Harry who looked equally terrified, 'It’s good that you learned the information, but facing a dragon is not an easy task. Many don’t live to tell'.
Many don’t live to tell – an echo in Harry and Astoria’s mind.
'You’re going to fight a dragon!?', she snapped when the realization came, turning to Harry who looked as if he didn’t have it in himself to react.
'Yes, he will', Moody answered for him, 'We will work more with him on this. Let’s start with you'.
Astoria instantly regretted speaking. When bravery pushed her to face him, to speak, to do any minor action that could keep her dignity – he made her regret it. A man that truly stroke fear in his opponent’s heart. And Astoria turned with shaking legs wondering what to do as his opponent now.
Harry stepped back, visibly uncomfortable himself.
'Hit me with something', he commanded.
All she remembered from dueling lessons with Lockhart was how to put her feet in the correct stance. Astoria lifted her wand, but before she even thought of a spell to cast, he jumped towards her, grabbed her hand and twisted her wrist. The wand fell of her hand as she screamed in pain.
'You’re so slow I could kill you even without magic!', he shouted at her and pushed her back.
Her back crashed into the wall. She whimpered from the pain, her face red with shame and with anger.
'Are you seeing red already?', he joked.
Fear held her tongue back.
'Disarm him', Harry whispered next to her.
That worked as her fingers quickly found her wand and snatched it off the floor. Alastor Moody didn’t seem please and stopped to stare at her with such – disgust, one might say, if appropriate.
'You should use your hands. This is how you will fight me'.
'What?', and the wand fell from her hand following the defensive charm Expelliarmus that gave her a reply.
'It’s an old technique, quite outdated, yet hard to dodge during a fight. You could say it could be your advantage.'
'No one fights like that', she blinked again with the feeling she forgot to study and do her homework. An annoying embarrassment that came with being ignorant.
'Your ancestors fought like that exactly because no one else did. How do you counter an attack you have never seen before? How do you adjust in a duel to an opponent who moves completely unexpected and new to you?'
Ancestors, the words spinning in her mind.
'I-, I can’t do it', her voice shook as she stood there awkwardly.
'Then you die', Moody cut her off as he lifted his wand.
The spell landed on her chest. Air forcefully left her lungs as she struggled to catch it back. It hurt. Her chest, her head too. And the pain just grew into a dry scream.
Harry gasped but froze with one look on Moody’s side.
'You’re weak', he spat at her, 'You’ve been weak for a long time'.
The pain felt good, Astoria realized. It made her angry. She couldn’t get up, but she didn’t need to. She blew off the hair in her face and her dark eyes met his. Her hand pushed forward, and the words fell out of her lips – Bombardo.
An explosion erupted in Moody’s office. Things started falling off the shelves. He, however, was intact. Bad aim. Astoria tried to get up, but Moody smiled sadistically at her. He was enjoying this and seeing it made her angrier.
'Pain, so you like pain?', he said as he grinned, 'Oppugno'.
All the objects on the floor headed towards her. Astoria tried to doge them, but she failed to do so.
And then their eyes met. He was furious. 'You’re like a snail. So slow and no backbone.' he shouted.
Astoria couldn’t do anything. She stood there in pain and tried to move only to fall again on her knees.
'Pathetic', he said as he sighed. 'Crucio'.
When you use one of the unforgivable curses, you must mean it.
Her mind went blank with pain. There was no sensation quite like it, nothing to compare it to so the mind could understand it better. Harry shouted behind her, or at least she imagined so, as Astoria heard his voice distant. Maybe it was a dying wish. Her whole body shook in pain and she screamed again and again.
'Concentrate on my voice', Moody shouted at her, 'Catch me with your eyes and try to repel it'.
She listened. It wasn’t hard as they were standing in a small room, but the pain was a constant distraction and her mind couldn’t ignore. It took a while. The more time passed, the harder it became to reach back for control. She saw him, but her eyes couldn’t hold him in place. The pain was eating her alive.
You’re going to die like this, a foreign voice whispered in her mind.
The though sank through her mind and she suddenly saw him clearly. Her eyes dark with rage. As her hands twitched from the pain she flinched and two of her fingers pointed at him. She hit him and the cursed disappeared. Blood painted his clothes red from his shoulders. She cut him, wishing him dead.
Harry was gasping for breath next to her, pulling her up from the floor. She rose on her feet. Moody seemed satisfied. The Cruciatus Curse was broken.
'We will continue to work from there, though I think outside will be better than this small room', he said out loud but didn’t look at either of them.
Moody was quick in healing himself and Astoria realized that all of her effort didn’t even leave a scar. As his body approached her, she flinched back from instinct. He gave her a hand, but she just starred at him.
'Good, savor the rage', he said to her with a smile and then looked at the door, 'you can go, Harry stays'.
Breathing hurt. She was going to be late, but she couldn’t run, she could barely walk for a fact.
He cursed me, she realized and stopped. There was an echo of the pain running through her whole body, as if her bones were music strings who still vibrated. Tears pushed trough her eyes. Astoria wasn’t sad, she couldn’t quire figure out why she was crying.
Her hair was a mess. She pulled out the braid and left her hair loose to try and make it better. Then managed to limp to Slytherin’s common room. A few eyes turned on her, but everyone was preoccupied. Draco and Pansy were dancing while Snape guided them with his voice.
He noted what an excellent pair of dance partners both of them were and gave them as an example. He also didn’t spare Astoria from a sharp look of disapproval when he saw her stepping in late.
Astoria could barely stand on her feet at this point. The pain grew weak, but she still felt it. Her muscles twitching beneath her skin. Theo Nott came to her. He tried to say hello, but his smile disappeared when he met her eyes.
'What’s wrong?', he whispered in her ear.
'I’m going to fall any moment now', she confessed to him.
His arms immediately grabbed her as he took the weight of her body on himself. Theo was strong and she almost got lost in him. He kept her standing and she sighed with relief as this somehow eased her pain.
'You look like someone beat you up', he commented and she noticed worry in his tone.
'Moody wants to train me. It was our first lesson and he cursed me', she said, panting for breath. Her face was covered with her hair as it had spilled over her from behind her ears. He gently pushed it back.
'Cursed you? Cursed you how?' he kept asking in disbelief.
'Theo, I’m going to fall', Astoria gasped.
His hands were on her waist. He pulled her closer to himself and held her like that until her body was able to push away the feeling of torture. It was a hug and it lasted quite a while. A few students gave them curious looks. Blaise snorted at Theo and Astoria felt ashamed she caught that but did not step away.
Theo had hazel brown hair, two dimples on the side of his mouth that appeared when smiling and strong arms. It had something to do with Quidditch, Astoria was sure, she just couldn’t explain it as this was another subject she was ignorant of. One thing that was sure however was that being in his arms felt bloody good.
When was the last time someone held her like that? When was the last time a boy took interest in her? One time, in the muggle world. Dumbledore had business, she was passed from one caretaker to another. They were in a café. When she went to the bathroom a boy followed and asked for her number. That was new to her, no idea what a number even was and she blew her chance with him completely.
Another muggle boy, her first kiss stolen on vacation. Something she did, not out of love but out of shameful feelings like the desperation to feel wanted and insecurities.
This wasn’t like that. Astoria wanted to thank Theo but could feel the redness on her face and was too ashamed to look back at him.
'Have you considered my offer?', he said suddenly.
'Yes, I have no idea why you want to go with me?'
'I think you’re nice', he said and smiled back.
'Cheating on Potter?', Blaise chuckled as he came near them.
Astoria pulled back and managed to stay on her feed on her own. Faced him. Blaise had beautiful dark skin that always had a perfectly healthy glow to it and almost perfectly symmetrical features. He always gave the impression he knew that as his confidence was intolerable.
'I think he’s out of the picture', Theo said with a smirk.
Harry had just defeated a dragon and his luck had changed as everyone was cheering for him again. Astoria’s luck had changed as well and wherever she was, she noticed a group of students from Drumstrang following her and eyeing her.
One on the left, three behind, a few, maybe five, staring across the corridor, one waiting in front of her. Just when panic made her think some of them followed her, she saw Harry. He was standing alone with Hermione. Astoria rarely stopped next to him, especially when her or Ron where around but she hadn’t seen Harry in a while. Sometimes the need to speak to him and be around him was undeniable.
'You can do it', Hermione said to him with a gentle smile, 'If you don’t, you will regret it'.
'You are right', he agreed with her. He did notice Astoria and smiled awkwardly at her, 'Wish me luck', he told her and she smiled back.
He left them there and headed towards a group of Ravenclaw girls. In that moment Astoria realized the crush he had on a girl from another house wasn’t her. It was Cho Chang, a Ravenclaw. He asked to speak to her and the two of them left the other girls, who giggled behind them.
'I’m sorry you had to see this', Harmonie said softly.
Astoria looked at her with suspicion. She knew none of Harry’s Gryffindor friends liked her.
'I don’t know what you mean', she responded coldly.
'Maybe its for the best', Hermione continued, 'I think you will put him in danger one day'.
She swallowed that. It was something Astoria feared herself, yet it felt like a smack on the face coming from her mouth.
'I still don’t know what you mean', Astoria barked back.
'I researched your family. They were all dark wizards. All of them. Did you know that?', Hermione said, she had this smart-ass tone that everyone around her barely tolerated mostly because she was also almost every time right. 'Even if you prove to be an exception, the chance of one of your family members being alive and finding you puts Harry in a position of danger and could give Voldemort a path to reach him'.
Astoria remained silent, thinking about what she was hearing. They were all dark wizards, she repeated in her mind with horror.  
'I agree', Astoria admitted quietly.
'Then you understand why you need to stop seeing him', Hermione was firm in her voice. Their eyes never met; both had a stoic look that never met the other. Harry was still speaking with Cho somewhere behind the corner.
'I think Ron’s insecurities are also a liability, would you cut him off too?', Astoria hissed. It was a test and she already knew the answer.
Maybe she just wished she was included, equal to them in a way in the status of 'friend of Harry'.
'No', Hermione answered and a long paused followed, 'Ron is one of us'.
'Then tell your boyfriend to leave me alone as well', Astoria said, her voice filed with malice.
She wanted to hurt her back. Her eyes met for the first time those of Victor Krum who followed her around like the rest of the boys from Drumbstrang. Now he stood around the corner, watching them talk, and he looked at Astoria as if he could jump in and kill her any moment now.
'They follow you on the orders of Igor Karkaroff. He thinks Voldemort is a threat no more, but is convinced you are, or you will be one day, a bigger threat to the magical world', Hermione stated dryly.
'I can barely do anything', Astoria confessed, knowing it wasn’t the smartest thing to do.
'Harry says so as well, yet the potential in your genetics is terrifying. Something common for pureblood families Is the strive to achieve the perfect wizard through breeding and magic. Your family line Is the only one that came close to success. Proving through generations, no matter how many were skipped, that every time an all-powerful wizard would appear' Hermione looked towards her for the first time.
She was already suspecting her of malice and betrayal.
'I’m not a pureblood witch, I’m just an orphan', Astoria said so quiet, it came out as a whisper. 'Like Harry'.
Harry was coming back to them; he didn’t show an expression on his face which meant he probably got rejected. When he was happy, the feeling couldn’t be contained in his body.
'He isn’t just an orphan and I think you aren’t either', Harmonie said sharply and headed towards Harry.
Astoria didn’t wait, she left immediately. She changed directions and headed towards Slytherin’s common room. Following the stares down a shadow caught up to her. And fear moved her as she turned to point her wand only to find Draco Malfoy next to her.
'Are you mad?', he said and Astoria sighed with relief. She wasn’t in the mood to exchanges unpleasantries.
'I’ve had a horrible day', she snapped, 'please don’t make it worse and leave me be'.
'I might actually make it better', he responded daringly, his eyes glimmered as he smiled towards her.
'Yes, by leaving me be.'
'Come', he commanded as he grabbed her by the arm and led her astray.
His grip did not allow resistance. They went down some corridor as faces on the paintings followed them. There were small, peculiar places, not exactly rooms but still private enough as walls crossed strangely in the dungeon, seemingly to confuse whoever once inhabited them.
He finally stopped and leaned towards the wall. He studied her with a cold gaze. Astoria found it hard to maintain eye contact with him as Draco’s eyes were icy and so light-blue it made her uncomfortable. As a child a caretaker told her that people witch such light blue eyes can hex just with their gaze. It was absurd, yet she shivered a little.
'I saw Theo Nott snooping around you', he finally said.
Astoria nodded as she didn’t wish to explain herself to him.
'What did he want with you?'
'We were discussing a potion in class, you were there', she said coldly.
'Why do you lie to me?', he hissed at her, visibly irritated. Astoria was ready to protest, when he caught her off guard. 'What about during the preparation for the Yule Ball, he talked to you then, held you even'.
Astoria stood there speechless. He saw, she thought with surprised, and then corrected herself – he watched. She looked back at him and forced herself to meet his gaze.
'He helped me stay on my feet. I am to train with Alastor Moody and it was our first session if you must know.'
'Fuck, what did he do to you?', Draco smirked and his face changed as he looked amused.
'He performed the Cruciatos curse on me', Astoria said slowly yet with confidence.
The smile quickly died on his face. Draco stood silent and looked at her for a while.
'I’m sorry he did that to you'.
'Is that all you talked about with Nott?', he finally said, softer than before. 'I thought he asked you to the Yule Ball?'
She hesitated for a moment, then finally said – 'He did'.
'Did you say yes?', his question followed immediately.
'I didn’t have the chance', Astoria replied with anger in her tone as she looked at him.
This seemed to give him some satisfaction. He suddenly leapt from the wall behind him and came towards her. As he got closer the taller he became, looking down on her.
Arrogant bastard, she swallowed.
Astoria took a deep breath yet remained silent. It was Harry she was hopping to go with. But Harry wanted Cho. She probably turned him down. Did she wanted to go with Harry that way? As the second-best option? No.
Reality lured her back as there was the sudden realization his face was next to hers. Draco’s eyes glimmered as he saw her return to him. She tried to step back but for every step she took, Draco took a step forward until he cornered her to the wall.
'Why would I do that?'
'I want you to tell him you’re going with me', he said slowly as a command.
'You?', Astoria was startled. She couldn’t comprehend what was happening. It was too random, too unusual.
'Yes. Me', he growled at her, leaning closer to her.
'But you don’t like me. You think I’m pathetic and you’re going to go with Pansy anyway', Astoria snapped at him and tried to push him away with her hands. He quickly restrained her and his face became hard as stone.
'Who said I don’t like you?'
'Why? God, why?', her voice grew louder, which apparently irritated him.
He quickly managed to grab her left arm by the wrist and his other hand he put on her mouth as he pushed her towards the wall to stay still. He turned to check behind him but shadows passed by and disappeared.
There were stars spinning in her mind. His body was next to her, his face was next to hers and she could feel his warmth. It felt strange, being so close to him. She met him every day in class, but he never stood this close to her. And this was no other than Draco Malfoy, the boy who made fun for her for years and who hated her friend Harry.
There was no point in keeping her quiet by force, as words wouldn’t come to her anyway thanks to shame. They never touched, actually no one ever touched her. It was Harry who used to hold her hand, but he always pulled and they rarely hugged because it felt awkward. Her body however seemed relax. It was her mind that was on fire. She was sure her face was red as a beet.
'Please keep it down', Draco hissed at her, as he looked behind himself once more.
His leg was between her legs, nonintentional, she concluded, yet it was all she could think about.
'You’re a Slytherin, yet you are never loyal to your house. I told you I can teach you some things. Besides, you, as just you, are fine. ', he hissed.
Is this supposed to be a compliment, she wanted to scream at him, but his hand was still pressing her lips shut. There was no point in trying. She just looked at him. Her free arm rested on his chest to push him away, but she didn’t, feeling his heart beat, steady with no trace of nervousness. It was a hypnotizing rhythm.
'I want you to go with me, just give me an answer', Draco said, he sounded as if he was striking a business deal, professional and cold.
His hand left her face and the word slipped out of her mouth almost immediately.
He looked surprised and so was she. Astoria didn’t even had time to think about it, honestly, she probably couldn’t think right now.
Draco didn’t move, not yet. His body stayed pressed to hers, his hand now resting on her neck. He studied her again with his cold eyes. She tried to look away, but he didn’t let her. It was a punishment, starring at him.
He is handsome, she realized taking in his image. But he looked repulsed as if she had offended him deeply. When he was satisfied with looking at her red face and watching her struggle next to him, he quickly released her and turned away. He didn’t even give her another look and just left her there, panting and gasping for breath.
The same night Astoria met Harry. She split her braids and she slipped out of her dorm. It was the last time, she told herself. Hermione was right, but she could say goodbye and have a last laugh with him. There was no harm in it.
Harry greeted her with a smile. He seemed clueless and happy, as he usually was. It was a naiveness to his manner that made him very charming. He made life seem easy and carefree, as if all the bad things truly never lasted but just passed by, while this warm feeling remained. It was an illusion, a coping-mechanism of his, Astoria guessed.
'How was your day?', she asked.
'Good, there are some things I want to tell you', Harry said as his smile shortened.
Suddenly the realization came – there was a smile on her face as well. It was a contagious happiness that Harry carried. And Astoria was happy to see him, to be able to share with him. It was hard to let go.
One. Last. Time.
She flinched back but tried to maintain the smile.
'I don’t know if you will like this, but we did some research on your family', he said slowly.
Harry was being cautious, preparing her, starting slowly. He almost looked like he was worried for her, which surprised her as she feared a hatred would grow in him once he knew. But apparently, he did long before her.
 It was logical Hermione would tell him first, probably warn him to stay away, Astoria thought.
'I know that they’re mostly dark wizards', Astoria said calmly.
Harry looked surprised. He looked through the window and tried to rethink what to say. Now she noticed he was a bit tense, his arms crossed over his knees in a defensive way, rather relaxing.  
'I’m sorry, I was worried how you’d react. You seem...fine?', he said confused, then his eyes widened with horror. 'Not fine, but you know, not crying'.
He felt like he fucked up. Tried to come close to her, to smile apologetically. All this was adorable to Astoria because he just wanted to protect her from the truth. She needed that from time to time as no one really protected her in life. Dumbledore was always away, though being in a way under his wing surely meant protection she couldn’t comprehend at this moment.
With Harry she could be vulnerable. She could finally share her true thoughts and not fear. He did judge her sometimes, he had just prejudices towards Slytherins, but he cared for her, in that she was sure and that mattered the most. 
Astoria laughed.
'To be honest with you, I just don’t believe it. I don’t believe I have anything to do with those people.'
Harry remained silent. So, she continued.
'I know that it passes through generations, some kind of power that is foreign to me. I think I’m just not the right generation. I think I’m just unlucky and not some kind of dark wizard waiting to emerge from my skin and –  I don’t know, take over the world or whatever', she laughed yet her eyes watered with tears she luckily managed to hold back.
'That doesn’t sound so bad', Harry said softly.
'I think so as well', she agreed, and a tear escaped, rolling down her cheek.
It was a lie. Elroy was a dynasty, a pureblood family that could change her social status, her confidence, everything about her life. But she tried to reject such notions in her mind. A cruel reminder that they left her behind as an infant. Even if she was some lost child, they didn’t want her in the first place. She was already insignificant to them and all that genetic greatness was lost on her.
But she wanted it. Even for a second, if she could dream, she wanted the power. To feel safe, to feel untouchable. And to be special, to be someone. Like Harry. But Harry was no great wizard thanks to his genes, he was great because he was brave and he pushed himself to be this way.
 It was a choice, Astoria thought, acknowledging that the same choice was probably an option for her as well through her life, she just chose like a coward.
Harry reached out to her and wiped the tear on her face. Her whole body shivered under his touch.
'You look beautiful', he suddenly said as both looked up in shook.
Astoria took a sharp breath that stayed in her so she could contain those words in herself forever. Harry looked back; a bit startled.
'I like your hair like this', he said, sighted and then added, 'I guess we’re both very lonely'.
'I’ve been lonely my whole life', Astoria answered but she wasn’t sad. 'It’s sometimes better that way. At least it’s true'.
'No, I just, I wish to enjoy things in the moment. Maybe for a little, even if it’s temporary. I feel like I might not live that long and I wish to enjoy it', he said in one breath, staring at her, realizing he probably spoke nonsense but it didn’t matter.
Astoria felt an empty space in her chest ache as she touched his shoulder for comfort.
'I want to go to the Yule Ball, would you like to come?' he added.
She did expect it, there was no surprise in that question, yet it still left her stunned. An answer didn’t come to her. That was unexpected. This is all she ever wanted and it felt wrong. Her stomach twisted itself and words got lost. She felt as if she was going to vomit. It wasn’t how she wanted it. His words seemed more like a cruel joke than those of Malfoy’s as she knew them to be untruthful.
'I-', that’s all that came out of her mouth. Harry stared at her, both with worry and with sadness, 'I already agreed to go with someone', she finally finished the sentence.
Harry seemed surprised which made her angry. As if she couldn’t go with anyone else because she was so undesirable. He always viewed her like that. Like a 'plan b', or 'plan c' matter of fact. It would’ve been great to go to the ball with Harry who was a champion for the Tournament. And he was going to be nice to her. All his Gryffindor friends would be pissed, so would the Slytherins who would never forgive her.
The next morning, she left her hair down for classes. It was going to be a pain in the ass, but she knew it made her look better as her hair framed her face. All she could think about was how she managed to get three proposals for the Yule Ball and fuck up all three of them.
This was the day of truth for Astoria. She frankly didn’t want to go with any of them.
Theodore was a liar, she knew, and his sudden interest in her probably had an interior motive that wasn’t just sleeping with her. He wanted to use her, she feared but she couldn’t say for what. The same could be said for Draco Malfoy and worse even.
Malfoy was a prick. But going with him would save her the bullying. He was also handsome and that sure would help make the night tolerable. And Harry just wasn’t an option considering she wasn’t a real option for him either, rather just back-up.
They had class with Alastor Moody. He was showing them how to stun someone effectively in battle rather than just make them dizzy. In other words, the goal was to completely knock out the opponent. It seemed like an aggressive spell and some Gryffindors were alerted by it.
The two facing each other were Pansy and Hermione. They could barely stand each other and the genuine anger they put into their magic did wonders. Moody was very pleased when Pansy fell down unconscious and then they spend the rest of it trying to wake her up.
When class ended the boys helped Pansy to recover. They took care of their own, that was at least undeniable about Slytherin. You could be awful and annoying like Pansy, bullied and used, but they would come for you and still lift you from the floor.
Draco held her hand as she tried to stay still. They previously dated in third year. For a bit, though at the beginning it was very flashy. He held her hand, took her everywhere, she kissed him in the hallways and one time they even got detention for inappropriate behavior. However, Draco changed and he grew colder towards her. There was a girl named Angelic, who was from Ravenclaw, he kissed once in the hallways but that seemed short-lived.
Sometimes he would snap rudely to girls and Astoria wondered if she ever got off his good side, would he talk to her the same way he did to Pansy who clearly loved him with undeniable devotion. It was pitiful, she took all his anger and swallowed it, while he never seemed to appreciate it. Love makes a fool of us all, so this time she couldn’t be a fool and had to choose with cunning.
If she went to the Yule Ball with Draco Malfoy, Pansy would kill her. But Pansy was a bitch and she deserved it, Astoria thought as an evil grin appeared on her face. It would also make Harry hate her, but that was somewhat the point, if it was hate or jealousy, she’d take it.
Astoria quickly caught up to them.
'Hello Astoria', Theo greeted her pleasantly once he noticed her.
She nodded with a smile and then turned to Draco. That warm smile faded into coldness and anger as she faced him. They all stopped. Pansy looked annoyed to see her, while Draco remained expressionless.
'I want you to know we have a deal', she said.
Everyone looked confused, even Draco raised an eyebrow.
'That was no deal', he said coldly as he glared her down with anger. He shook off Pansy’s arm that held him and put his in his pant’s pockets. 'Come', he commanded and once again she obeyed.
As they walked down the corridor, they passed Harry and his friends. Astoria saw the look of disbelief on his face and the sharp looks Hermione and Ron gave her.
They think they’re finally right. They think to themselves 'See, she really is a Slytherin, one of them.' I am, I really am, Astoria told bitterly to herself, but it felt like victory.
Draco Malfoy had this effect, he made you feel important in his presence. You could just tell by that, that he was a pureblood, an aristocrat to the wizarding world. He was raised to command respect.
'I don’t think you understand the definition of a deal. I am to get something out of it, and the way I see it I am just at a loss', he said coldly and didn’t even bother to look at her.
For all those years in Hogwarts Astoria concluded that Draco Malfoy’s amazing superpower was always looking extremely bored when talking to others or being in their presence. They always felt inferior to him, as did she in this moment.
'I am open for a discussion. Whatever you want, you can ask it of me', she said yet her voice trembled because she didn’t really mean that.
Desperation pushed her to say things she didn’t truthfully mean. She had little to give and when she imagined what a boy, not Malfoy, but just a boy – could ask from her, well, she shivered.
He stopped and looked eyes with her. People passed them in the hallway.
'Let’s go somewhere private', he said.
Her legs moved on her own following his lead. They found themselves in an empty classroom for potions class. This already felt illegal to her.
'What If prof. Snape comes?', she asked with fear.
'He brews his potions in his own office. Privately', he explained, and she stared at him surprised he has this knowledge.
Maybe because he was clearly his favorite student, that was a normal thing to know. She had no more time to spare on this observation as she turned to face him and realized it was time to explain herself.
'I want to go to the Yule Ball with you', she said confidently and forced herself to look at him.
He seemed amused by that. He smiled, not a sincere and large smile like Harry’s. Malfoy was always smirking as if everything was ironic to him.
'What made you change your mind? Potter finally rejected you?', he spat at her.
'I rejected him, actually'.
'If you lie, I’ll know', he warned her as the distance between them narrowed.
If I lie, he will know, she repeated in her mind. Yet this only gave her more confidence in herself because she was telling the truth. Her legs moved and she faced him.
'It’s the truth. I don’t want it to be him. And if you reject me, I will go with Theo', Astoria said, trying to spare him as many details as possible.
'Don’t threaten me', he rolled his eyes.
Draco walked in a circle around her. Watching her from every corner. Insecurities pushed in her mind, but she quickly blocked them mentally because this could be a tactic on his side. To make her weak, to make her slip. He stopped behind her and Astoria quickly turned to face him again. It was important not to be intimidated by him. It was time to be brave.
'You only answered one of my questions. I still don’t know what made you change your mind', Draco reminded her.
Sometimes he sounded like a smart-ass as well, she thought with irritation.
'I want what every girl wants. To go to the ball and dance with someone handsome. To have fun. To feel pretty. You could give me that.'
'I could', he made a step forward, 'What could you give me?'
'Anything', she said with a deep breath as he came closer.
'Be careful now', Draco warned as he pointed a finger at her, 'you could gamble away all your aces in one turn'.
'I’m horrible at gambling', Astoria confessed.
'You are', he agreed coldly. His face remained mostly expressionless though she could see he was amused.
'You could demand anything from me. I realize this could be an inconvenience to you so I will do my best. Whatever you want me to do, to wear and how to look – I will agree.'
'Your low self-esteem is so unattractive', Draco spat at her. She took the offence and swallowed it as she kept looking at him determined to have her way.
There was a long pause in which he looked at her up and down.
'I like your hair long. What dress are you wearing?', he finally added and sighed, which she interpreted as agreement.
'White with silver lining on it. Short.'
'Short', he repeated as he smirked, 'I like that'.
Astoria took the comment as a slap on the face but didn’t flinch. She never knew him to be a pervert, but she knew him to be a sadist and a bastard. Maybe he was going to find a way to humiliate her, to make her regret this. As doubt began clouding her thoughts, she took a step back without realizing it. Her eyes found his black shoes coming closer and closer to her. As she looked up his hands were already on her neck, pushing her chin up. His thumb resting on her face.
'You are so naïve. So easy. This might be a bad deal for you', he whispered next to her skin.
'I want to do it', she said firmly.
'You want to be bad?', Draco Malfoy chuckled, 'That’s so unusual of you'.
' I –', she lost her words and before she could say anything he let her go. He walked out of the room fast and didn’t even turn to look back at her.
Agreeing to go to the Yule Ball with Draco Malfoy turned out to be a bad deal for Astoria. Somehow her luck was worse.
The news made the boys from Drumstrang only suspect her even more of some kind of evil intent. Pansy wished her dead and didn’t even try to hide it. All the Slytherin girls thought she had somehow seduced Draco Malfoy, which was an absurd notion, and that she stole him from innocent and in love Pansy. They punished her for this with gossip and conspiracies about her family.
Like all gossip, word got out. Harry passed her through the hallways and refused to even look at her. His face was always cold, his jaw tight. He felt betrayed. Malfoy was, in a bit dramatic way to say – his enemy. They could barely stand each other. And she chose him over her best friend. Her only friend. The choice seemed more stupid with each day that passed.
Theo also seemed unhappy with the spreading news. He did try to court her, gave her a rose in class which made her face go red and she almost fainted under the stares she got. As his efforts proved pointless because there was no way to go against Malfoy and win, Theo eventually gave up on her. Rather easy, to her disappointment.
In contrast, Malfoy barely gave any thought to her. He continued his everyday life as before. Barely interested in her, barely looking at her. Of course, Astoria didn’t expect anything else from him, but it only made her suspicious. And his behavior was the reason why some people suspected she even made this up and lied. This only gave her reason to fear she was being played. Maybe it was all an evil plan to hurt her and thus Harry.
Maybe Malfoy wouldn’t even show up. Or he will show up with Pansy. Maybe he would just leave her alone all night. Astoria sometimes had nightmares like that as the days to the ball shortened.
The only relief was that the mean jokes stopped. Pansy would occasionally be a bitch to her, but she was careful in her words. If Astoria was really Draco’s, insulting her now meant insulting him and that was something to rethink in Slytherin.
All the looks and all the whispers behind compensated and made her nervous. That’s why Astoria decided to go on a walk in the snow. Autumn had already slipped away, and Winter came beautiful in white. She carried a book with her.
She passed near Hagrid’s. Harry had taken her there once during her second year. Hagrid knew her from Dumbledore and mostly looked at her with curiosity, but he was never cruel to her. Neither cold like Dumbledore. He was nice to her and once called her a 'sweet girl'.
Tears pushed through her eyes. She wiped them aggressively as she got angry at herself. She quickened to the forest and found a nice spot to rest a little. As she took a deep breath, she heard a branch snap.
She turned in horror only to find nothing. Astoria felt silly, paranoia had taken the best of her lately. The forest was beautiful and empty mostly in this part. If you went deeper – sure, something might attack you. But this was castle territory.
'Elroy', a quiet voice spoke.
She turned and saw three boys from Drumstrang approach her. They circled her like wolves. Oh god, she realized with fear that this was an ambush.
The book fell from her hand, and she took out her wand. One of them laughed.
'We just want to talk', he said as his steps towards her gave out the lie in his words.
'I’m not what your Headmaster has told you I am', Astoria said, her voice suddenly rusts in her throat.
'I think that only makes it easier', the boy in the middle laughed.
They were only a few steps away from her. And she realized how much taller and stronger they were. Large frames. Muscles. They all looked like that, and she figured their studies required physical training as well. How could she be a match for that?
Suddenly the spell Moody thought them came to her. She didn’t hesitate to think it through. Her wand pointed to the laughing boy in the middle as she stunned him. He fell on the ground. Knocked out. The other two boys looked surprised for a second, yet that was enough for them, and they didn’t hesitate no more. It got serious.
The first blow landed.
The tension between them was gone starting a domino’s effect. They both ran to catch her, and she screamed, turning to run away. A red light passed her. A spell. They missed this one. The next one got her. Imobulus, she heard with horror behind her as her limbs froze and her face crashed in the snow.
They could beat her. They could rape her. They could kill her. She was, again, helpless, useless –
Astoria tried to scream but a hand pushed those screams back to her throat. She could now see him clearly. He had a buzzcut, a scar on the nose, small but deep. He had blue eyes, dark blue, not like Draco’s. And he was smiling at her, grinning his teeth like an animal. Like a hungry wolf.
'Stop, god, please', she screamed.
He twisted her braid on his hand like a chain and pulled her hair as her whole body rose with it. A hard punch landed in her stomach and a scream got lost in her mouth. Air left her lungs forcefully. It hurt. Like Moody’s hit. That spell. She couldn’t remember and there was no point.
'An Elroy', the boy with the scar hissed in her ear, 'What a catch'.
'Do you know your ancestor, whatever he is to you, has killed thousands of my people', the boy who landed the punch squatted Infront of her. His eyes meet hers.
He was blond. Again, a buzzcut. Again – taller and larger than she could ever be. His eyes were black, consumed by rage as he kept talking. Looking at her as she cried.
'My grandfather lost all his family because of him. He burned them alive. He ate some, even', he said with disgust and spat at her. She tried to turn her face, but the other held her still.
'I don’t know who those people are', she shouted, and another punch hit her body.
Her vision got blurry. Everything was going dark like a sunset. Her mind somehow cleared, and a loud voice echoed.
Astoria opened her eyes with surprise as adrenaline somehow filled her. The two boys were still holding her down. One held her arms, the other was still pulling her hair. The blonde one had his hand on her face, his fingers sinking in the hollow of her cheeks.
'What?', she repeated confused.
'I said you need to pay!', he screamed in her face. Spit landed on her skin as she closed her eyes again.
Simple-minded creatures. Like animals. Punish them like ones –
It was a man’s voice. It hissed at her. It sounded amused, excited. She tried to look away, to locate this man. Why wasn’t he helping her? She couldn’t see, her eyes flooded with tears.  Simple-minded, she repeated to herself.
A green light hit the blonde boy behind her. A scream came somewhere in the woods. She ignored it. The other boy was dragging her deeper between the trees. He pushed her behind a tree and put a hand on her mouth. His eyes met hers.
Simple-mined, she realized and wanted to laugh. A smile crept onto her face, and he looked at her confused.
She could feel him. It was a new feeling. Different. She could feel him as his skin touched hers. She could see in him.
In this moment a door opened. It was like he himself invited her in. So easy. She walked through it.
Astoria’s eyes rolled back. So did his. They both froze with blank stares. It was dark. She was in his mind. His name was Georgy. He had a sister that was dead. His mother was beautiful. He thought about them now as he was feeling terrified. She put that fear in him.
Command him to release you-
'Release me', the words echoed in their combined consciousness.
Her body felt the warmth of his touch leave her.
Tell him to kneel-
'Kneel', she obeyed the voice who grew stronger, boiling with excitement.
Tell him to kill himself-
She felt two hands grabbing her by the shoulders. Someone screamed in her face. Astoria blinked and she could suddenly see. Harry’s scar, his messy hair, his skin on her skin. He looked afraid. What was he afraid of?
She grabbed his hands as he pulled her up. She rose to her feet. Hermione was standing next to him, her hands resting on her knees as she struggled to catch a breath. Astoria looked around and saw fiery-red hair. Ron was standing next to Gregory that looked as confused as she was.
Harry’s words were starting to reach her.
'Did he hurt you?', he shouted at her.
'No', she whispered. Her body was a bit heavy, but her mind felt like a sinking stone.
'She hurt me! She was going to kill me! It wasn’t me!', Gregory shouted as Ron restrained him.
Harry looked angry but not at her, Astoria realized. Hermione approached her, her finger touched the pulse on her neck.
They don’t believe him, she thought with relief.
'How did you-', Astoria lost her words.
It was like her mind was putting itself back together. Organizing itself again like a shelf with books that was struck by an earthquake.
'We saw a man lying on the snow and we went deeper in the forest. That’s when I heard you scream', Harry said quickly as he pushed her body to his.
He hugged her. They hugged once, before. During second year. Lockhart revealed himself. Hermione was gone. Ron was going to follow Harry to find Ginny. They thought they were going to die in the Chamber of Secrets. He didn’t let her come. He hugged her then.
'Where did he hurt you?', Harry shook her a bit.
That’s when the pain struck. She let out a scream. Finally, the realization came to her that there was blood dripping from her mouth.
'He punched me in the gut', she said in one breath.
Hermione pushed back Harry and quickly did a diagnose on her with her wand.
'Internal bleeding. This could be bad. We need to get her medical help immediately', she said at Harry.
Astoria felt his hands around her. Her feet left the ground. Her mind was still a mess.
'Did you find him? The man?', she asked.
'Yes, Ron will report them', Harry said through his teeth.
'Not them', Astoria said quietly but had no strength to explain. Her eyes never landed on him but she heard him, felt his presence.
There was someone else.
They let her go after three days before the ball. She felt fine. The nurse told her to avoid too much physical activity, to not lift heavy things, and to sit down if she got tired. Dancing was allowed, she specifically asked.
When she got back to class no one asked her anything and she left before someone could. Dumbledore wanted to see her after the ball. They had a scheduled meeting. Finally.
Apparently, there was a scandal. None of the boys from Drumstrang continued following her and stalking her. They were forbidden to come near her. Victor Krum did once on the hallways and simply said 'Sorry'. They never spoke again.
She had nightmares constantly. In fact, she was going mad but if she told someone, they would put her in a white room or force her to stay in the nursery for months and she wouldn’t go to the ball. What a selfish and stupid reason to keep a secret, she thought.
But Astoria remained loyal to her desires.
The voice would speak to her in her mind. Telling her she needs to grow stronger. Telling her they all hate her and would kill her if given the chance. She shivered in fear more often now then before.
Theo Nott stopped her in the corridor. He looked sad as he looked at her. Her braid was messy. She didn’t have the time and her hands shivered still. Astoria knew she looked tired and sad and beaten up.
'Are you feeling better?', he finally said, looking at her with those big eyes that shined between charming brown curls.
She hated the feeling of being pitied. It filled her with so much rage she wanted to scream.
'Yes', she said coldly.
'They got what they deserved', he said with a smile, 'I want you to know it was taken care of'.
She blinked at him.
'A few of us talked with them about the incident. They will never even look at you again', he said and came closer to her.
She flinched back as an instinct. Her books fell from her hands. He picked them up and hanged them to her. People watched.
'I’m sorry, I know you probably need time', he said and pulled back.
'I don’t', Astoria hissed.
Theo swallowed as he didn’t know what more to say. He was going to leave when she looked up to find his eyes and grabbed his hand.
'What did you do?', she asked.
God, she wanted to be the one hurting them back. Revenge felt like a forbidden desire that slipped in her mind more often than she would ever to admit.
'We take care of our own, Elroy', Theodore’s eyes darkened. Astoria felt as if she saw him for the first time as he really is, 'I think you’d like to know that'.
She didn’t say anything. She just nodded and moved away. She didn’t want to know that.
Astoria spent every night looking at the window in the castle’s ceiling. She was sure if she looked hard enough, she could find the place where they ambushed her. She didn’t want to admit it, but she took a liking to the voice inside her head. It made her feel powerful and that helped to heal her pride from the humiliation she suffered.
Whispering horrible propositions to her.
Harry appeared one night. It was a risk but after their fallout Astoria did not expect him even though he rescued her.
'I didn’t call for you', she said surprised to see him. It was unusually late for their meetings. Tomorrow was the Yule Ball. Everyone was probably asleep, so they’d look fresh the next dat.
'I couldn’t sleep', he said sounding tired.
'Me neither', she sighed and then added, 'I suppose I never got to thank you for saving me'.
Harry sat next to her. His jaw tightened and he looked angry, she feared it was her fault again.
'I’m sorry I didn’t come earlier', he said bitterly.
'It’s okay', she lied as she hoped this would make him feel better. He looked at her, his eyes still sad. It didn’t work.
'I heard you had your own battles to fight with some magical egg', she said, trying to change the subject.
'Yes, Cedric told me as I told him about the dragons. It was a fair exchange. He’s taking Cho to the ball', Harry said.
Astoria remained silent. She was afraid he’d remember her betrayal, and all would be ruined. That seemed to be the case because he did seem angrier now.
'I don’t know why you agreed to go with him', he finally said the damn words.
'He wanted to go with me and it seemed genuine', she said sincerely though she actually had doubts in that statement.
Malfoy did give her looks of concern in class but kept a distance. Pansy circled around him but that wasn’t knew. And it was the least of her cares. It was the fear of being played and humiliated tomorrow that bothered her.
'Maybe it is', Harry said softly. Astoria looked surprised at him.
She didn’t like this. He accepted it and this only meant Harry now saw her as a true Slytherin. As someone different from him. And she wasn’t. She was just like him. An orphan. An unfortunate child. An Elroy. No –
'Are you okay with that?', Astoria said and then quickly added, 'It’s just a dance for one night. It’s not like me and him are close'.
'I can’t stand him', Harry replied, maintaining his control over himself, 'But I know he found the boys that hurt you and he hurt them back. Him and others. Then he made it all go away. I suppose that’s not my style, but it was right by you'.
Violence will only bring more violence, she thought bitterly. There was an even scarier phrase a caregiver once told her – 'Put your sword back in it’s place, for all who draw the sword will die by the sword'. It was biblical, from a muggle religion.
The woman was kind, and she gave her a cross to wear for her birthday even though she didn’t. She also told her that angels looked out for her.
Astoria got back to the conversation.
'I didn’t ask for that', she finally said, 'I don’t think I would'.
Harry smiled at her.
'You are good, Tori', his voice sweet like a melody. She shivered. Was there ever someone as kind to her as he was?
'With whom are you going to the ball?'
'Parvati Patill', Harry sighed. Clearly this wasn’t his wish.
'She’s a nice girl', Astoria added, though her words were dry and somehow got lost in the silence.
At least she could always be silent with him. There was comfort in that. She knew she didn’t excite him the way other girls did. She knew she was too shy, too unusual for him, but she hoped he felt safe with her the way she did with him. Harry was always there. He wasn’t a great friend but was a sincere one. And Astoria felt the same could be said for her as well.
'Hermione told me she thinks she could be wrong about you', Harry added after a long silence.
'She might actually be right', Astoria said coldly. 'Those boys thought so too'.
'They were in the wrong', his words filled with anger.
'Dumbledore has requested to speak with me'.
'I’m surprised it took him so long.'
'He once told me he deeply cares for you'.
'Only half of him cares for me. The other half is restricted to himself. You should know he is like that', Astoria said, her tone ice cold.
'I think he means good'.
'Whatever the definition of good is in his mind, probably, yes', she rolled her eyes.
'I’ll always be here if you need me', Harry said softly. His chest hurt. That’s the only thing that came to mind.
Things would be so much easier if she was a Gryffindor. If she spent her nights laughing with him, Ron and Hermione while listening to Fred and George poke fun at someone or tell stories about their glorious pranks.
They shared almost half of their classes, but he never felt as if she was there with him. There was always a wall that Astoria put between herself and others. He never knew how to tell her that.
'I’ll always be here if you need me', Astoria repeated his words and smiled at him.
The boys were instructed to wait for the ladies. Astoria was terrified. What if he finds her unattractive? Such a stupid fear, yet it ate her alive. She was amazed with herself. Since when did she care if Draco Malfoy found her attractive?
Actually, she really cared.
Her dress was white with silver lining around the tips of the dress. There was a touch of silver sparkling on her chest and on the lines of the dress. The emphasis of the dress was on the waist where the material perfectly hugged her body. It was a short dress, like he wanted it.
Her hair was down, curled nicely by magic. It was hard to keep her hair from her eyes as it spilled everywhere around her body, but she could take it as long as it made her look beautiful. And that’s all she wanted to feel tonight.
Am I pitiful?, she shook her head and headed down the stairs to meet him.
Draco Malfoy wasn’t looking. Crab and Goyle stood around him like bodyguards. Theodore was there as well. He already had his lady of the night. Pansy, she realized with surprise.
Draco wore a classic black suit. He wore the color more often now, Astoria weirdly observed. Theodore smiled as he saw her, taking her image in his eyes and then pushed his friend on the shoulder so he would turn. His eyes landed on her and pierced her.
Draco didn’t react, he didn’t even smile and that hurt her.
What a fool I am, she bitterly thought trying not to demonstrate her disappointment around Pansy who was already looking at her up and down. She wore a long black dress that sparkled. It looked great with her short black hair. It made her seem taller and elegant.
Blaise Zabini came around the corner with Ginny who took all the attention in a beautiful red dress. All of her was on fire. But she was a Gryffindor and a Weasley which instantly turned heads among the Slytherins. That was an opening and Malfoy lifted his hand forward to greet her. Astoria took him by the elbow. His blue eyes met hers.
They stepped into the ballroom. It was beautiful, white with light and flowers. So many flowers, Astoria immediately felt intoxicated by the sweet smell. A smile appeared on her face as she looked around. Unconsciously her fingers tightened around him. Malfoy noticed and looked at her, but she didn’t. Her attention was consumed by the beauty that surround her. Her feet felt light and she could almost say she was excited.
He led her to a table that was also covered with flowers. There were drinks around them. This wasn’t a table for two. As Astoria looked around she noticed the tables were for six people and others came in, filling the room and finding their place.
Their table had a beautiful view towards the dance floor. That’s when she realized with horror she’d had to dance. She never did. She didn’t remember was there ever an opportunity to do so, an invitation maybe? Even if there was, she probably turned it down and now she was left with regret.
'You look sad all of a sudden', Malfoy commented, carefully observing her. She realized that as she turned to face him.
'I just realized I don’t know how to dance', Astoria confessed.
'This might be a problem', he said. 'As we are about to dance a lot tonight'.
Before she could say anything, a chair was pulled next to her. Theo Nott sat there and beside him Pansy Parkinson. The table was in the form of a circle so they could all see each other. Later came Goyle with his date – another girl from Slytherin named Athena. She wore a short blue dress with purple flowers on it.
The room was filling with more people. Colorful lights glanced around them. The Headmasters came, all dressed in official wizard robes. Astoria turned so she wouldn’t have a chance to meet Igor Karkaroff’s gaze. Fear slid in her body as suddenly she was in the forest and a boy was pulling her hair.
As she closed her eyes to take a breath a foot punched her under the table. She looked around with surprise to meet Draco’s eyes. He was serious, almost angry, staring her down. It was so she’d behave. Astoria understood and nodded slightly to show him that.
The champions of the Tournament had the first dance. Cho Chang and Cedric Diggory passed. They made a beautiful couple. 'Horrible seeing your ex with a cheaper version of you', Pansy said to her. It was an obvious low-blow.
Astoria turned to her. She forgot how it was, how it always was with them. The constant need to put the other down. The competition. The battle for power.
'Keeping your bloodline pure is about more than who you fuck', Astoria said to her. Pansy’s mother was from muggle descent. You could say she was mixed.
Everyone looked surprised. It was the first time Astoria used her supposed heritage like that. She knew this stung Pansy as she turned elegantly and raised her glass of wine. It was a good explanation to imagine Draco asked her because she was like him – pure-blooded. Was she though?
'Since when are you more than an orphan?', Pansy said with a hollow laugh that gave away her insecurity.
Some other couples started going to the dance floor and the night began. It was a slow song. Draco didn’t ask if she wanted to join. He got up and opened his hand so she’d take it. And Astoria obeyed.
'It’s a rare find, someone who’s your equal', he said so they’d all hear.
They went deep into the crowd. His arm pulled her by the waist. His body was against her.
He’s handsome, a thought pushed through her consciousness. His blond hair was beautifully put together. His clothes fit him perfectly and he was tall. The pale skin, the blue eyes that seemed more grey under the light. As if he was a marble statue, but he wasn’t cold like one.
'Watch your feet', Draco said coldly.
'I’m sorry', Astoria quickly responded and swore to pay more attention to the moment than get lost in thoughts.
'Lean on me', he said and she listened, 'Good girl', he added as her face blushed. He was making fun of her. It was his part of the deal.
Dancing was easier when he was the one who had the lead. He had perfect control over his movement and of her. His grip was tight. Astoria relaxed, even if she were to fall, he would catch her on time.
'I never got to ask. How do you feel?', Draco said. It almost sounded to her as concern.
'I’m okay. Thank you', she said and nervously added – 'for what you did'.
'You’ll be safe from now on'.
His hand twisted as he spun her gracefully. He did that again after a few seconds and Astoria couldn’t help but smile. It was all she ever wanted. To be beautiful and to dance with a handsome boy.
This time he pulled her back with more strength, she didn’t resist as she landed on his chest. Touching him was exciting even though it was through clothes. That made it safe and excusable.
'You look like you’re having fun', Draco sounded surprised.
'Shouldn’t I?', a sudden concern slipped in her voice as she looked at him with fear he might take it away.
'Be my guest', he said and for the first time she saw him smile as well. It was a pleasant smile. It made his face glow up and warmed him immediately, as the ice melted away.  
'You never told me', she said between gasps of breath, 'Why did you want to go with me?'
'You’re fishing for compliments', Draco said irritated by that, but without anger. He is having fun as well, Astoria realized and hoped to be true.
'Please, spoil me', she whispered in his ear. It was naughty and not very smart of her to do so, but it made her laugh.
'You look beautiful tonight', he said with a deep breath as if it costed him to say it.
'You didn’t answer my question', Astoria whispered again, insisting.

He was pushing back. It was an instinct as Draco made a small step back. He didn’t want to talk about it, she figured, but she didn’t care. Her steps were now the dominant one. 'You’re an Elroy', his face suddenly buried in her hair. She could feel his warm breath against her skin, 'That made you vulnerable'.
'It matters? You wouldn’t ask me if I wasn’t whoever everyone thinks I am?', she shook her head to get away from him. He immediately stopped that intent.

Malfoy’s hand grabbed her waist and pulled her back to himself.

He smirked as his hand held her tight. Astoria wanted to run. He was mostly right, she bitterly realized. Her ignorance of the problem only made it worse and it made her weak. Open for attacks. 'I remember what you asked of me and I can deliver. I will dance with you and I will make you feel good', Draco responded slowly and then suddenly changed the topic, 'Do you want wine?'

Astoria looked at Malfoy who was grinning. She couldn’t focus on Pansy, her mind a chaos trying to figure out what had just happened. He was being awful to her. He called her an idiot. He was cruel to her. Did they not see that?

Draco Malfoy was suddenly standing next to her. He leaned over the table and looked down on her. His tie a bit loose, a flush of redness on his cheekbones.

Dumbledore’s Army, he realized. It was something very new. At its core - him, Ron and Hermione as well as a few other Gryffindors that wanted to rebel against Umbridge’s tyranny.

The girl’s bathroom. No one was there, not ever. Astoria opened the door and then summoned a locking spell – 'Colloportus'. Just on time as the click of the lock moved, she let out a loud sob. But that release was temporary and her body quickly froze as her eyes saw a shadow move.
